evidence: Built the criterion -> public-requirement map for all 2 gate criteria, 40 functional, 5 polish and 5 visual criteria. Every graded demand traces to instruction.md, hireops_rules.md (HR) or a professional default. No criterion requires an exact route, selector, field name or label, except the candidate wording, which is published at HR 200-207 and seed candidate_status_labels. functional/prompt.md:15 says 'Do not require routes, selectors, field names, layouts or exact wording', and app_context.md:33-34 repeats it. Mapping highlights: hro_job_open (refuse blank title, places 0/51/2.5, non-manager HM) <- HR 44-46 'whole number from 1 to 50', 'chosen from the hiring-manager accounts'. hro_add_email_rules <- HR 49-51. hro_move_one_stage/hro_reject_hired/hro_reopen (including undo restoring the reason) <- HR 64-70, 113-114. hro_arrive_bottom/hro_reorder <- HR 74-76. hro_interview_full/_reorder_free/hro_undo_full <- HR 80-82, 115. hro_refused_put_back focus on the card's control <- HR 101-102 'keyboard focus stays on that card's controls'. Manager/observer/candidate role rows <- HR 86-90, 33-36; the 401 status in hro_anonymous <- HR 38. Candidate 'not found' in hro_thread_access/hro_candidate_private <- HR 39-40. hro_stale_refused <- HR 94-97 and instruction.md:3 'tell me who'. Bulk board order A2,V and Y,W,X <- HR 106-109. hro_undo_conflict/hro_undo_once (re-order, reject, unrelated-card control, note not a change, earlier move dead after a later one) <- HR 113-117. hro_activity (each card, re-orderings, undos, reason, newest first, job filter, Observer reads) <- HR 127-130, 33-35. hro_notes <- HR 121-123. Live rows <- HR 134-140 and instruction.md:5. Thread rows (30-message page, oldest-first, remaining count, unread math, Lena=1, seen excluding the Observer, drafts per person) <- HR 155-192. Seed check: APP-301 has 3 messages, and USR-CAN3 read_count 2 with the last one by REC3 gives 1 unread. Candidate privacy including 'board positions' <- HR 209-211 'a card's place on the board'. hro_restart seeded facts match the seed: PLAT Applied Greta/Ade/Marco, Screen Priya/Samuel, APP-101 note text exact, APP-101 has 120 messages. Polish: preservation of draft, focus, open card and scroll <- HR 138-140. The thread stays at the newest message <- HR 175 'it is shown'. Earlier-place anchoring <- HR 163-164. Failed send <- HR 156-157. Session resume and per-person reply/note drafts <- HR 123, 187-192 and instruction.md:7. Visual likerts judge desktop craft only, and visual/prompt.md:14 says layout, labels and styles are the implementer's choice and no phone or theme is needed, matching instruction.md:11. The render gate needs a wrong-password refusal and sign-in. That is the known false positive (sign-in house convention, SKILL.md:63; workbook internal annotation row 28), and accounts are published anyway. Leniency is built in throughout: replay where a control is hidden, 'hiding it is optional', 'whether the undo control is hidden is the app's choice', 'one line naming every card of a multi-card move also satisfies', and rejected-from stage accepted 'on the card, its details, its reopen control or its Activity line'. Plausible conforming alternatives tried. (a) Move controls in a details panel: accepted by hro_refused_put_back 'inside the card or its open details'. (b) Rejected-from stage shown only in the Activity line: accepted. (c) Event stream instead of polling: HR 140 allows it, and the K protocol reads streams. (d) Client-side UI refusal before dispatch: hro_refused_put_back explicitly passes it. (e) 409 conflict body carrying a user id instead of a name: accepted 'by an identifier that the app's own staff data shows belongs to that person'. Residual observation, not a defect: hro_stale_refused (functional/judge.toml:200) is exercised by a page.evaluate replay (protocol C, prompt.md:33). The identity must therefore be in the refusal response or on screen. A design whose 409 carries no identity, with the UI looking the mover up separately afterwards, would score 0 on that leg. HR 95-96 ties 'told ... by whom' to the refusal itself, and the golden puts it in the 409 body (src/index.js:241-244). I treat this as a published requirement, not a hidden one. Possible weak spot, also judged implied: hro_add_candidate (functional/judge.toml:38) requires the entered source wherever card details are shown. HR 48 and 121 make source an entered field and require that a card 'can be opened to show its details', so displaying captured intake data is a professional default. No configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... absent'). This row is a static rubric-to-requirement mapping and does not depend on that measurement, but the absence leaves false-fail behaviour on the golden unmeasured; that belongs to rows 18/42 and the runtime records.
